items.title: The normalised gaps of the scale-invariant point process follow a GEM distribution
items.author: Tony Haddad; Dimitris Koukoulopoulos
items.work: On Arratia's coupling and the Dirichlet law for the factors of a random integer
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled proposition at source lines 706-709: the vector formed by one minus the first gap and the successive later gaps, all divided by the logarithm of x, follows a GEM distribution. The proof (source lines 711-713) is a single change of variables, but the step is not formal: the scale-invariant spacing process has to be transported by the map sending s to the base-two logarithm of x minus the logarithm of s, the mapping theorem has to be invoked to know that the image is again a Poisson process, now homogeneous of rate one on the whole real line, and the ordered points of that process have to be recognised as producing the geometric proportions that define the GEM distribution. The statement records only the resulting law.
